inputs.share_count_basis: 998m shares outstanding at 2026-08-02 (Q2 FY2026 10-Q balance sheet) plus ~2m dilutive equity awards (diluted weighted average 996m vs outstanding 998m; 1-2m anti-dilutive excluded) = 1,000m. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting as well would double-count. No non-SBC issuance expected (SRS/GMS/Mingledorff's were all-cash).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K (HD_Annual_FY2026.txt:3057) cash-flow add-back $522m. HD publishes no combined SBC+equity-award-tax figure; tax withheld on net-share settlement is not separately disclosed and immaterial (equity-statement repurchases $0-26m/yr), so the add-back is used alone.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Cost of equity 8.9% = 4.3% 10y UST + beta ~0.95 x 4.8% ERP; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.6% (3.5% after 24% tax) on ~$53bn; market-value weights ~86/14 at a $343bn equity cap. WACC ~8.2%, used as 8.25% in all three scenarios. Housing cyclicality and acquisition leverage are priced in the scenario flows and the 20% bear weight, NOT as a WACC premium (risk charged once), so WACC is identical across scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Under US GAAP (ASC 842) operating-lease cost sits in SG&A, so reported EBITDA and OCF are already after operating rent; operating lease liabilities ($1,516m current + $8,155m long-term at 2026-08-02) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance-lease liabilities ($3,094m) sit inside current installments/long-term debt and stay in total_debt, with their principal outside the flows -- one treatment each, never both.
inputs.nci_treatment: None material; HD has no non-controlling interests.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route), routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md as a US operating company that is cyclical (housing/remodel) with material leases, so owner-fcf.md + adaptations (b) leases and (f) risk-once applied. No prior DCF or memory entry; fresh build. PERIOD LABELS: the Metrics CSV labels HD's fiscal 2025 (52 weeks ended 2026-02-01) as FY2026; fy0 = FY2026 (CSV) = fiscal 2025, revenue $164,683m. Year 1 of the projection is HD's fiscal 2026 (ending ~2027-01-31), for which guidance exists. ANCHORS: net debt = short-term debt (CP) 4,248 + current installments of LTD 4,697 + LTD 43,951 - cash 2,085 = $50,811m at 2026-08-02 (latest 10-Q). OWNER FCF: reported FCF 16,325 OCF - 3,679 capex = 12,646; minus SBC 522 = 12,124 (levered, after ~$2.2bn interest). HD is net-debt, so no interest income is stripped. FY0 FCF is depressed by tax timing (FY2024 Q4 federal estimate deferred into FY2025 under hurricane relief) and is NOT the projection base: the forward build is unlevered and component-built (year-1 owner-FCF margin ~9%, vs 7.4% levered FY0 and a 7-12% levered history). BUYBACKS: paused since March 2024 to delever after SRS ($18.25bn) and GMS (~$5.5bn); $0 in FY2025 and none guided for FY2026. The flat count is a modelling convention HD is not currently funding; the SBC charge is small (0.32% of sales) so the gap is ~0.3% dilution/yr at most. EBITDA BASIS: ebitda_margin_path is GAAP operating income + cash-flow D&A (incl. intangible amortisation) + SBC, i.e. pre-SBC; FY0 = (24,404 + 522)/164,683 = 15.1%.
inputs.guidance_fy2026: Reaffirmed at Q2 FY2026 (Aug 2026): net sales +2.5% to +4.5% (incl. GMS annualisation and Mingledorff's), comps flat to +2%, adjusted EPS flat to +4% off $14.69, capex ~$4bn (~2.5% of sales), no buybacks. H1 FY2026: sales +5.3%, comps +1.2%; ~$685m of IEEPA tariff refunds credited to COGS (one-off, not carried forward).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity/book CAGR is not usable: stockholders' equity was negative in FY2020/FY2022 labels and swung from $1.6bn to $12.8bn in three years purely from buybacks pausing (treasury stock $96bn). Equity CAGRs computed mechanically (102% 3y, 31% 5y) are artefacts and are set null; revenue 5y CAGR is selected instead.
historical_growth.notes: Periods are CSV labels (FY2026 = fiscal 2025; 3y base FY2023, 5y base FY2021). FCF CAGRs are on the owner (SBC-adjusted) series. Owner-FCF CAGR (2.9% 3y) runs slightly below reported (3.2%): SBC grew 12%/yr (367 -> 522) against ~1.5% revenue growth, so a modestly rising share of comp is paid in stock. The 5y FCF CAGR is negative because FY2021 (pandemic) FCF of $16.4bn was a peak; FY2025 is also tax-timing depressed. Revenue 5y CAGR includes the SRS (FY2024) and GMS (FY2025) acquisitions; organic comps were roughly flat to -3% over FY2022-FY2025.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 3.5% = midpoint of the reaffirmed 2.5-4.5% sales guide (GMS annualises in Sept 2026). Y2-Y5 4.0-5.0%: a gradual remodel/turnover recovery off a multi-decade-low housing-turnover base plus SRS share gains and bolt-ons, roughly the 5y revenue CAGR. Fades to 3% by Y9-10.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: FY0 pre-SBC EBITDA margin 15.1%, down from 17.4% (FY2022 label) on deleverage and SRS/GMS mix. Y1 14.9% strips the ~$685m one-off IEEPA tariff refund (~0.4pp) from an otherwise flat-ish H1. Recovers 0.9pp by Y7 on comp leverage, still below the FY2023-FY2024 15.6-16.2% because distribution mix is permanently higher.
base.capex_rationale: Guided ~$4bn / ~2.5% of sales for FY2026; 2.4% Y1 on the guide over a 3.5% sales base, 2.4-2.5% thereafter (FY2019-FY2025 range 1.9-2.3%, rising with the new-store and SRS branch programme).
base.da_rationale: Cash-flow D&A $3,514m = 2.13% of FY0 sales, including ~$0.6bn amortisation of SRS/GMS intangibles.
base.tax_rationale: Unlevered cash tax at HD's normal ~24% effective rate (FY2025 cash taxes $4.85bn); no carryforwards or one-offs to ramp.
base.wc_rationale: Inventory-heavy retailer/distributor: receivables + inventory (~$33.8bn) exceed payables + deferred revenue (~$16.3bn), net trade WC ~10% of sales, so growth consumes ~10c per incremental $ of sales (negative capture).

scenario_narratives.base: Housing stays stuck but stops getting worse: turnover recovers slowly from multi-decade lows as mortgage rates drift down, repair/maintenance holds and big-ticket remodel returns only gradually. FY2026 lands at the midpoint of the reaffirmed guide; SRS keeps taking share in fragmented specialty distribution (roofing, interior products via GMS, pool, landscape, now HVAC via Mingledorff's) and adds bolt-ons, lifting sales 4-5% a year mid-decade. Margins recover about 0.9pp on comp leverage but never regain the FY2022-FY2023 peak because the lower-margin distribution mix is permanent. Leverage is worked down and buybacks resume late in the period, which this model treats as value-neutral.
scenario_narratives.bull: A real rate-cut cycle unlocks pent-up turnover from the 'locked-in' mortgage cohort and an ageing housing stock: comps run mid-single-digit for several years, the Pro ecosystem (Pro Xtra, trade credit, SRS cross-sell into HD Pros) converts into wallet share, and the SRS roll-up compounds. Operating leverage and a stabilised mix take the pre-SBC EBITDA margin back to 17%, the FY2023 level. Growth is ~6-7% for three years before fading to 3.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Housing rolls over rather than recovers: a consumer/construction recession produces a 2008-style (if milder) sales decline of ~3% in FY2027, with transactions falling, big-ticket projects deferred and Pro trade-credit losses at SRS. Deleverage plus tariff cost re-imposed under a non-IEEPA authority (no refunds this time) push the margin to 13.2% at the trough, and the permanent distribution-mix dilution caps the recovery at 14.3%. Elevated debt from SRS/GMS keeps buybacks off and the CEO-leave/integration period goes badly. Growth recovers only to 2-3.5%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): housing is genuinely cyclical, the balance sheet is more levered than at any point in the last decade after SRS/GMS, and tariff policy is unresolved -- but there is no solvency or refinancing risk (A-rated, ~2.6x net debt/EBITDA, $14bn+ net income). Base 50%: guidance is reaffirmed and H1 is tracking it. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): the bull path needs a rate-driven housing turnover recovery AND a margin return to FY2023 levels, two things HD does not control.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Unlevered owner-FCF DCF on a component build, 10-year horizon, SBC fully expensed and share count flat, WACC 8.25% identical across scenarios with housing-cycle risk carried in the scenario flows and weights. Terminal value is the lower of Gordon and a cap (18x base, 20x bull, 15x bear) appropriate to a mature, cyclical retailer. HD is a high-quality compounder, but at the current price the market is capitalising a lower discount rate and/or a fuller margin recovery than the base case grants.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount rate: value is highly sensitive to WACC on a terminal-heavy, low-growth stream; each 50bp is worth roughly 8-10% of value.
Margin recovery: every 0.5pp of terminal pre-SBC EBITDA margin is worth roughly $15-20/share.
Housing cycle timing: a recession in FY2027 (bear) versus a rate-cut-driven turnover recovery (bull) is the dominant swing factor.
Acquisition mix: further SRS bolt-ons add growth at lower margins and are funded with debt; the model includes no future M&A cash outflow while counting the growth only in the bull case.
Leverage and buybacks: buybacks are value-neutral here; a resumed buyback at prices above IV would destroy value relative to this model.
